Executive Order
Mrs. Stella Davis Mudd may be reinstated as an operative in the Bureau of
Engraving and Printing without regard to the length of her separation from the
service . Mrs. Mudd resigned as printer's assistant from the Bureau on February 9 ,
1909. Her reinstatement by executive order is recommended by the Secretary of
the Treasury in view of the fact that Mrs. Mudd is a widow with four minor
children to support . The Civil Service Commission is unable to concur in the
recommendation .
Done for charity .
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
November 3, 1925.
[No. 4332]

Executive Order
In consideration of the services of Lieutenant Commander Louis Collins
Scheibla , United States Navy, who died as an officer on active duty and in the line
of duty when the seaplane , in which he was flying as an observer , crashed into the
Potomac River near Dahlgren , Virginia , on April 17, 1924 , his widow , Mrs. Belle
Barrick Scheibla, may be employed in any clerical position under the Navy Depart￾ment which she is qualified to fill, without regard to the Civil Service Act or Rules .
Mrs. Scheibla was appointed on July 7, 1924, under the Executive Order of
June 27, 1924, on the rolls of the Veterans' Bureau for duty in the Navy Depart￾ment for work in connection with the administration of the Act to provide adjusted
compensation for veterans of the World War . Her present employment will soon
terminate , owing to lack of work . The Secretary of the Navy states that she has
demonstrated her ability to perform satisfactorily such clerical duties as have been
assigned her , and , in view of this fact, it is desired to retain her services under the
Navy Department .
The Civil Service Commission does not concur in this recommendation .
Done for charity .
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
Νου. 7, 1925.
[No. 4336]
CAL

Executive Order
By virtue of the authority vested in me by law, Paragraph 12 of the Executive
Order of February 2, 1914, ( No. 1888 ) , providing conditions of employment for the
permanent force for The Panama Canal, is hereby amended so as to authorize pay￾ment to certain hourly and per diem employees for emergency work in excess of
eight hours on Sundays and authorized holidays , on the same basis as now auth￾orized or may hereafter be authorized for employees of the Naval establishment
in the United States. As amended , the paragraph will read as follows :
12. Employees above the grade of laborer , appointed with rates of pay per
hour or per day, will not be employed over eight hours in any one calendar day,
except in case of emergency . The time such employees work over eight hours in
one calendar day, and time worked on Sundays and regularly authorized holidays ,
including January 1st, February 22d , May 30th , July 4th, Labor Day , Thanksgiving
Day, and December 25th , shall be considered overtime for which time and one-half
will be allowed. Such employees who work on the days prior and subsequent to
the holidays specifically named above will be allowed their regular pay for eight
hours for such days, in addition to pay for any work performed ; Provided , That
payment to such employees for emergency work in excess of eight hours on Sundays
and authorized holidays shall be made on the same basis as now authorized or may
hereafter be authorized for employees of the Naval establishment in the United
States .
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
June 17, 1926 .
[No. 4459 ]
CA

liquidated and there remains nothing further to be done than to pay the assets
thereof to its stockholder, United States of America ; and

United States Sugar Equalization Board , Inc. and of the officers and directors
